exposure: Age groups (13-16 years overall, with further analysis for ≤14 years)
outcome: Neonatal outcomes (1-minute Apgar score, NICU admission, birth weight)
cohort: 172 adolescent patients aged 13-16 years who delivered in two large tertiary hospitals between October 1, 2018 and April 15, 2022
finding: Anemia during adolescent pregnancy was associated with a higher risk of preterm birth, cesarean section, and low birth weight.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rate was higher in patients with anemia compared to the control group (45.31% vs. 38.88%, p < 0.001).
birth_weight: Low birth weight (LBW) was increased in the anemic adolescent group ≤14 years old.
